name: Agag
bio:
Agag was the king of the Amalekites. The LORD commanded Saul to go to war against the Amalekites and destroy everything they had without mercy, but Saul captured Agag alive and spared the best of the sheep and cattle, destroying only what was worthless (1 Samuel 15:1-9). The LORD told Samuel he regretted making Saul king, and Samuel went to confront Saul over his disobedience, declaring that the LORD had rejected him as king (1 Samuel 15:10-29).

Samuel then had Agag brought before him; Agag came trembling, saying, "Surely the bitterness of death is past," but Samuel said, "As your sword has made women childless, so will your mother be childless among women," and cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal (1 Samuel 15:32-33). Agag's sparing by Saul and subsequent execution by Samuel's own hand marks the decisive turning point that led to Saul's rejection as king for failing to fully obey the LORD's command.
